context: To maximize total value for a given capacity, use each unit of capacity for the highest unit value available. The greedy strategy for fractional knapsack therefore starts by sorting all candidates in descending order of unit value.
description: The center table lists items in descending order of unit value. The diagram gives the numbers in all four columns: item number, weight, value, and unit value. Fruit names come from the icons. Two labels read “Sort by decreasing unit value” and “Greedy strategy: choose items with higher unit values first.” A gray arrow on the right points upward toward higher unit values. Selection proceeds from the top row down.
The table follows the order in the diagram. The apple and grapes both have a unit value of 5. The apple appears first, but items with equal unit values can go in either order.

frames.explanation: Take each item whole if it fits. Otherwise, take just enough of it to fill the knapsack. In the earlier example with capacity 50, this means taking the whole banana and 30 units of pineapple for a total value of 277.5. That result comes from applying the rule to the earlier example. This diagram shows only how to sort and choose items.
frames.title: Greedy strategy for fractional knapsack

summary: Sort the items by decreasing unit value and take those with the highest value per unit of weight first.
